'''Nikko-in''' (日光院) is a [[:en:Koyasan Shingon-shu|Koyasan Shingon-shu]] temple located in {{ill|Yabu, Hyōgo|en|Yabu, Hyōgo|WD=Q869014|lt=Yabu|1=Yabu, Hyōgo}}, {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|en|Hyōgo Prefecture|WD=Q130290|lt=Hyōgo Prefecture|1=Hyōgo Prefecture}}, Japan. It is part of the Myoken-san complex and venerates {{ill|Myōken|en|Myōken|WD=Q10960623|lt=Myōken|1=Myōken}} (Myoken Daibosatsu) as its principal image. It is one of the "Three Great Myoken" temples of Japan.

== History ==
According to temple tradition, Nikko-in was founded during the reign of [[Emperor Bidatsu]] (6th century CE) by the monk Nikko Keiju, who established a hermitage at the site. 

In {{ill|1485|en|1485|WD=Q6644|lt=1485|1=1485}} (17th year of the [[Bunmei era]]), the temple received a land grant from {{ill|Yamana Masatoyo|ja|山名政豊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamana Masatoyo|1=Masatoyo Yamana|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11467585}}, demonstrating its historical significance.<ref>Yamana Masatoyo’s Myoken Shrine Land Grant (document held by Nikko-in) {{harv|Hyōgo Prefectural Archaeological Museum|2010|p=38}}.</ref>
